title: Lonnie Polk's band and the Eastern Shore guardian story
summary: The Polk band played similar jazz around Baltimore, Washington and the Eastern Shore. Waters, underage, needed a guardian trombonist and was caught with sand on his clothes after meeting a girl.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Back to Philadelphia in the late 'teens. Were there other orchestras that you would consider at least some of the times jazz besides the Miller thing? This man you mention, Lonnie Polk, what band -
What kind of music were you playing?
Well that was similar to Charlie, Charlie Miller, similar. Only Lonnie played a little bit more jazz. See, Lonnie -
You mean, Lonnie as an individual played more jazz than Charlie Miller -

So that made the band, in some respects made it a little bit, little bit better maybe, could have been. We did a lot of work in Baltimore, in Washington and down in the Eastern shores, see. I never forget that, Eastern shore. I mean, see, I was a - I don't know if I'm allowed to put this on this -
I am? Well in the Eastern shore I was [ ] in short pants. And my - ah, what-do-you-call-it guy who has to have charge when you go, when you're too young to work, to go -

Yeah, that's it, I had to have it. 'Cause I was a, I was not of age. So this trombone player - I forget his name too, it wasn't Driver, it was another trombone player, and he was more of a tailgate trombone player, you understand what I mean, he wasn't - he sounded much like Kid Ory, in that type, you know. So I forget his name right now - so he was the one that went to my aunt, got the papers from the police that he would take care of me, you know. See, so at intermission I met a little girl, see. And by the way, this little girl is livin' right here in New York, and I haven't - I didn't know, I haven't seen her, she's living right here in New York, I haven't seen her since I've been coming here, I guess she'd married somebody, I imagine. Anyway, I met her, you know how musicians, girls stand 'round you, you eyeball. So I went down in the, underneath the boardwalk, we were playing in the - I think it's Cambridge, if it wasn't Cambridge it's someplace on Eastern shore, near the shore, near water, see. Most of all those places are near the water down there, you know. See, so I'm in the boardwalk, and we were talkin' and fooling around, see. So I got a whole lot of sand on, when I came back up, you know. There was sand all over my clothes, see. So this guardian, the guy who was responsible for me, looked like that, you know, with big surprise, see. So I told him that I fell down (laughs). 'Cause I had never got really well, see, so that's easy to believe you, see. So I was brushing the, brushing off the sand off as I could, but it still was some left, see. So he - but he was nice, you know. See, they had a big to-do about it like, say "A young boy like you fooling around, I've gotta take more care of you", influences like that, see. Well, that band, we used to do colleges, we seemed to be popular in the Eastern shore. And then we also played in Jersey, then we played in Baltimore and Washington. Also with Charlie Miller, we played in Baltimore and -
So you would play outside Philadelphia -
with both Charlie Miller's band and with the Lonnie Polk band -
Yeah, sometimes. You know how it is, we were gigging. See, we had this - with Charlie Miller we had this regular gig three times a week and Saturday evening, Kater. But with the -
